pairs.complementarity.title: Complementary site pairs
pairs.complementarity.definition: For every pair of sites and each compared window: a_s and b_s are the times the window holds at each site; either_s at one of them at least; both_s at both; neither_s at neither, with its longest stretch and its intervals. gain_over_better_s is either_s minus the larger of a_s and b_s; covered_share_of_better_outage is that gain divided by the time the better site lacks. distance_m is the great-circle distance on the reference sphere.
pairs.complementarity.algorithm: Union, intersection and complement of the visibility windows of the site packages, each taken at its default observer height. The packages must share one time range.
pairs.complementarity.frame: local East/North/Up at each site; up is the outward radial direction of the reference sphere
data: the direction table of the site packages

evidence: core/tests/test_trade_pairs.py::test_mast_height_in_a_crater_against_the_closed_form: visible time for five observer heights against the closed-form rim elevation (threshold 5 s)
Both are arithmetic on the visibility windows and inherit their accuracy and their limits.

limits: The comparison says when at least one site sees the body. It says nothing about moving power or data between the sites: no line of sight between them, no cable, no relay is computed.
Each site's windows carry the limits of its own horizon.
